text.title: Ads Budget Optimization Examples
text.summary: End-to-end worked example for Ads Budget Optimization (scenario, traversal, draft artefact, validation outcome), then the working formulas and tables: target CPA, efficiency ratio, 70-20-10 tranches, reallocation decision matrix, diminishing returns, pacing, cross-channel comparison, a reallocation pass, incrementality outcomes.

example.title: Solo consultancy application
example.code: Input scenario: a faion.net solo consultant evaluating Ads Budget Optimization. Step 1 — gather inputs: source-of-truth + prior artefact verified accessible. Step 2 — apply core rules: each rule in 01-core-rules.xml passes; one rule flagged for remediation but not blocking. Step 3 — walk decision tree (06-decision-tree.xml): preconditions met; branch leads to a non-skip conclusion referencing the primary rule. Step 4 — draft artefact: all required fields populated; evidence cited per non-trivial field. Step 5 — validate + hand off: scripts/validate-ads-budget-optimization.py returns OK; status set to ready_for_review.
example.note: Artefact below validates against the JSON Schema in 02-output-contract.xml. Reproduce by running `scripts/validate-ads-budget-optimization.py --file artefact.json`.

example.title: Resulting artefact JSON
Target CPA from LTV
example.code: Average customer value: $500 Target LTV:CAC ratio: 3:1 Target CPA = $500 / 3 = $167

example.title: Efficiency ratio scale
example.code:
Efficiency = Target CPA / Actual CPA
> 1.0 → Beating target → Scale = 1.0 → At target → Hold < 1.0 → Missing target → Optimize or cut

list.item: 70% — Proven: campaigns with efficiency ratio over 1.0 for 3+ weeks
20% — Promising: campaigns that need optimization to reach target
10% — Testing: new channels, audiences, or creative concepts

section.title: Reallocation decision matrix

list.item: CPA 1.0-1.3x target: hold budget, optimize creative
CPA above 2.0x target: pause, rethink strategy

section.note: Increases are applied in steps of at most 30%, 3-5 days apart (scaling-increment-30-percent rule); the matrix gives the destination, not the step size.

section.title: Diminishing returns model
section.p: Expected CPA increase when scaling a single campaign:

example.title: Monthly pacing variance
example.code:
Expected spend on day X = Monthly budget * (Day / Days in month) Variance = Actual spend / Expected spend
Above 1.05: spending too fast, reduce daily budget 0.95-1.05: on track Below 0.95: underspending, check delivery issues

example.title: One reallocation pass
example.code: Current: Meta $5K, Google $3K, LinkedIn $2K — total $10K, target CPA $60 Meta: $50 CPA, 20% under target → increase to $6K (+$1K) Google: $75 CPA, 25% over target → decrease to $2.5K (-$500) LinkedIn: $133 CPA, 122% over target → decrease to $1K (-$1K) Testing reserve: +$500 for new channel test New total: $10K maintained

list.item: High incrementality: conversions drop when channel is paused → keep and optimize
Low incrementality: conversions hold when channel is paused → safe to reallocate
